It seems to me that there are a lot of defeq abuses in MonoidAlgebra, blindly identifying elements in a (additive) monoid algebra with terms in (M →₀ R). We have docs#MonoidAlgebra.coeff but this is not used in docs#AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree, for instance, that on my opinion should be defined as f.coeff.support.sup D; and similarly I think that docs#MonoidAlgebra.single should rather be defined as MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff (Finsupp.single m r).

This impacts in particular the abstraction barrier between supports of terms in monoidal algebras and in finsupps and reflects on the way we define both the degree of terms in monoidal algebras and of MvPolynomials. I would propose to make a more systematic use of .coeff and .ofCoeff. Any ideas (I'm pinging in particular @Damiano Testa and @Yaël Dillies )?
And these won't get solved when it becomes a one-field structure?

Yes, this is even better, because then we can keep the abbrev between AddMonoidAlgebra and MvPolynomial and for a p : MvPolynomial we would have p.support unambiguous as a term in an AddMonoidAlgebra instead that as a finsupp.
(modulo the slight problem that we don't yet have MonoidAlgebra.support but this will be easy)
@Yaël Dillies Do you see major obstacles with your PR that I can help with?
Related: do we agree that docs#MonomialOrder.degree should not live in root but it should become MvPolynomial.MonomialOrder.degree?

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Yaël Dillies Do you see major obstacles with your PR that I can help with?

No, no major obstacle. The situation is that there is a lot of defeq abuse in and around MonoidAlgebra. In #38714, I tried to fix the minimal amount of abuse to get CI passing, but oftentimes the easiest solution to something breaking was to rid it of its own abuse (so eg I am fixing docs#PolynomialModule in #38714 too, PR description will be updated once CI finally passes). Ultimately, fixing all the defeq abuse at once would work, but this is an unreasonable approach so one instead needs to push the boundary of abuse just a little past MonoidAlgebra.

Concretely for #38714 this means fixing the remaining files in whatever way possible, with little concern to how ugly or unmaintainable the new proofs are, because making these proofs better again will involve several orthogonal refactors that shouldn't be part of #38714.
I have asked @Erik (√2) yesterday if he could get his LLMs to fix #38714, but if you have manual fixes then please push them to the branch right away!
OK, thanks for the update. And do you have an opinion about why we have two folders about MvPolynomials, one in RingTheory and one in Algebra?
My instinct is to unify them (in RingTheory): they're not abstract generic algebraic objects, but really pertain to ring theory, no?

I do not have an opinion. But if you move MvPolynomial then surely you should also move Polynomial, MonoidAlgebra, SkewMonoidAlgebra?
